newsitem.title: UK: CBI to urge UK's Brown to raise taxes - BBC.
newsitem.headline: CBI to urge UK's Brown to raise taxes - BBC.

text.p: Britain's top employers' organisation, the Confederation of British Industry, will later on Tuesday urge Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown to put up taxes, the BBC reported.
A BBC radio report said the CBI would argue in its pre-budget submission, due for release later, that taxes needed to go up to dampen consumer confidence and stem inflation.
Brown will unveil his first budget on July 2.
Last week, Sudhir Junankar, the CBI's associate director of economic analysis, said the top employers organisation was pencilling in personal tax rises to the tune of two to three billion pounds.

After Britain's new monetary policy committee raised base rates to 6.5 percent last Friday, Junankar's boss, Kate Barker, said she wanted to see "a small fiscal tightening" in the budget, in order to calm the consumer sector.

"Consumer spending is likely to be pretty strong on the back of these very large windfall gains but exports are likely to continue to have a very tough time," said Barker, who is the CBI's chief economist.
"We hope therefore that further rate rises can be kept to a minimum."
Economists forecast windfall payouts from building societies converting into banks this summer could exceed 30 billion pounds.
